risks.risk: Any credential delivered to browser JavaScript is observable by the local user or a compromised trusted page.
risks.mitigation: Prefer trusted server exchange and narrowly scoped short-lived tokens; guest code receives no credential by default.

risks.risk: The isolated toolchain Worker permits JavaScript unsafe-eval because the retained Vite dependency-optimizer path requires dynamic code generation.
risks.mitigation: Never reuse toolchain Worker policy for ordinary guest code; strict guest CSP forbids unsafe-eval.

risks.risk: Current production evidence is Chrome 153 on Ubuntu 24.04 x64 CI only.
risks.mitigation: Do not claim cross-browser/Windows/macOS/mobile support until explicit campaigns exist.

risks.risk: No weak-device/thermal/memory-pressure production floor is currently proven.
risks.mitigation: Resource limits are enforced but performance/resource-floor claims remain open under P7/P15.

risks.risk: A reverse proxy/CDN can strip or alter CSP/COOP/COEP/CORP/Permissions-Policy after the app server.
risks.mitigation: Run hosting self-check and browser acceptance against final release topology before production claim.

risks.risk: Integrity-valid third-party package code may still be malicious within the capabilities granted to guest/toolchain execution.
risks.mitigation: Least capability, Worker isolation, lifecycle-script deny, package corpus review and dependency/security policy.

risks.risk: Future AI/provider adapters may introduce long-lived credentials or broader network authority if they bypass Core capability rules.
risks.mitigation: Keep AI/provider behavior outside Core until separately versioned adapter threat model and credential policy exist.

risks.risk: A future server broker could introduce SSRF if implemented as an arbitrary URL proxy.
risks.mitigation: Core has no broker; frozen broker requirements demand destination policy, redirect reauthorization and no arbitrary proxy.

risks.risk: Machine security courts and scanners cannot establish that the product is secure or replace independent/human review.
risks.mitigation: Keep P12-18 and P12-20 open until named second-party and human review evidence exists.
